A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GAINS by the same authors and retain the same underlying research framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, view-count analyses, and qualitative reconstructions on Synthetic4Relight, TensoIR, and Ref-Real.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the retained datasets and Shiny Blender, including new Stage I ablations and directional-relighting analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the two-stage framework but substantially revise its components. TV-only normal guidance becomes combined L1 and TV supervision, KNN floater removal supplements alpha-mask regularization, and Teamwork supplies IID albedo priors with RGB2X retained for outdoor scenes, replacing v1's exclusive RGB-X specification.

E1.justification: v2 adds Shiny Blender evaluation on reflective synthetic objects, extended with ground-truth albedo and relighting and excluding the ball object. This expands the evaluated object coverage. Synthetic4Relight and Ref-Real remain, while TensoIR is retained in Appendix C rather than removed.

E2.justification: Synthetic4Relight Table 1 adds evaluated GShader, R3DG, MaterialRefGS, and SVG-IR comparators to Ref-GS and GI-GS. Ref-Real's quantitative comparison also adds GShader and R3DG. Ref-GS becomes Ref-Gaussian but cites the same work; GIR remains a qualitative comparator.

E3.justification: Reported loss weights change: BCE from 0.1 to 0.75, IID from 1 to 2, and lighting TV from 1 to 0.1. The new Shiny Blender view-count study includes 64 and 100 views, beyond v1's 4–32 range. v2 also introduces Stage I experimental controls, runtime comparisons, and controlled 90-degree lighting rotation. These are reported setting and design changes, without independently establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds Stage I ablations of depth, normals, SDS, and outlier removal in Table 3, directional-shading and relighting-error analysis in Figure 6, and MI-SDS difference images in Figure 7. View-count sensitivity is revised and extended on Shiny Blender. Conversely, v1's segmentation-lifting sensitivity study using 25, 50, and 100 views and its separate toycar view-count analysis disappear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Variance terms in the method are regularizers, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many reported values and result entries change. In Synthetic4Relight Table 1, GAINS NVS/albedo/relighting PSNR changes from 30.23/22.97/25.582 to 29.32/22.34/28.16; roughness MSE changes from 0.026 to 0.04, while newly evaluated SVG-IR reports 0.03. TensoIR and Ref-Real scores also change. New benchmark, comparator, and ablation results accompany removal of extensive appendix results. These revisions accompany changed method settings and do not establish controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 4 mathematically redefines normal guidance from a TV term to a weighted combination of two L1 terms and TV. The principal BRDF, segmentation-consistency, and SDS formulations remain equivalent; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 identifies Stage II as the primary contribution; v2 explicitly positions integration of foundation-model priors with physically based representations across the framework as the core contribution. The abstract specifies competitiveness across 4–32 views. The central claims about complementary priors enabling sparse-view inverse rendering remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning ignored global illumination and wavy normals causing specular effects to enter albedo. It explains diffusion's artifact suppression and limited hallucination under late activation. The dense-view discussion replaces v1's segmentation-versus-fine-roughness tradeoff with an explanation involving Ref-Gaussian's appearance fitting and continued densification. These substantially revise mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies diffusion guidance scale 100, KNN removal every 1,000 iterations, and fixed hyperparameters without scene-specific tuning or prior fine-tuning. Appendix B adds preprocessing times and distinguishes offline priors, intermediate semantic processing, and diffusion active during optimization. It also revises reported optimization time from approximately 1.5 hours to 1 hour 20 minutes.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Relightable 3D Gaussian, Teamwork, SVG-IR, and MaterialRefGS, connecting them to evaluated baselines or the IID prior. The related-work narrative and sparse-view research gap remain largely intact. Ref-GS/Ref-Gaussian and RGB-X/RGB2X refer to retained cited works rather than new citations.

P1.justification: The seven-section main outline and much of the method exposition remain. Editorial changes include revised abstract and contribution framing, foundation-model terminology, clearer evaluation and ablation headings, baseline-name corrections, and condensed appendix discussion. Much of the added prose documents scientific changes assessed separately.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column format and substantially reorganizes its displays. Tables gain comparator rows, runtime and normal columns; TensoIR moves from main Table 2 to appendix Table 4. v2 Figure 5 combines a new view-count chart with the gardenspheres comparison, and Figure 7 combines quantitative and qualitative ablations. New error/shading panels appear while most earlier appendix comparison panels are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: broader comparator testing addresses v1's narrow comparisons, Shiny Blender tests reflective-object recovery, and Table 3 supplies previously missing evidence about Stage I components. Explicit limitations and computational details improve transparency. These benefits outweigh the loss of useful appendix sensitivity studies and examples. Some claims remain overstated: SVG-IR has lower roughness error in Table 1, and removing segmentation improves albedo PSNR in Figure 7 despite the blanket full-model superiority claim.
